annual-budget-and-millage.name: Yearly budget and property tax rate

ordinance-adoption.name: Passing a local law or policy

annual-budget-and-millage.name: Yearly budget and property tax rate (county and cities)
annual-budget-and-millage.summary: How a county or city sets its property tax rate and budget each year under the TRIM (Truth in Millage) law. The rate a body sends the Property Appraiser in July becomes, in practice, the highest rate it can adopt in September.
annual-budget-and-millage.dayCounting: TRIM periods count the later of July 1 or the value certification date as day 1 (s. 200.065(12), F.S.). Offsets here are calendar days added to the anchor date, so "within 35 days" is offset 0 to 34.

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for regular taxing authorities, Florida DOR

milestones.name: Budget calendar posted online
milestones.output: Public calendar of this year's budget steps

timing.rule: On or before January 30 each year.

residentCan.how: Use the calendar to put the workshop and hearing dates in your own calendar now.

milestones.influenceWhy: A schedule, not a decision, but it tells you when every later step happens.

milestones.name: Departments ask for money
milestones.output: Budget requests to the Manager or Mayor

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually winter or spring. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Tell your commissioner and the department head what service you want funded, before the request is written.
Ask for last year's department requests to see what was asked for and cut.

milestones.influenceWhy: Requests are still being written, but they are internal and not yet on any agenda.

milestones.name: Elected officials set budget priorities
milestones.output: Priorities the proposed budget must follow

timing.rule: Set by each body (a retreat, budget address or early workshop). Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Speak at the retreat or workshop if public comment is taken.
Send your commissioner one or two specific asks while priorities are open.

milestones.influenceWhy: Priorities steer the draft before numbers are fixed, but nothing is voted on yet.

milestones.name: Property Appraiser certifies taxable value
milestones.output: Certification of Taxable Value (Form DR-420) with the rolled-back rate

timing.rule: Assessment complete by July 1; this date (or a later certification date) is day 1 of the TRIM clock.

residentCan.how: Read the DR-420: it shows how much taxable value grew and the rolled-back rate (the rate that raises the same money as last year).

milestones.influenceWhy: A valuation by the Property Appraiser, not a policy choice by the body.

milestones.name: Mayor or Manager presents the proposed budget
milestones.output: Proposed budget and recommended tax rates

timing.rule: Set by the county charter and code or the city charter. County: the Mayor prepares it June 1 to July 15 and presents it no later than the day the Commission sets tentative rates.

residentCan.how: Read the proposed budget the day it is posted and note the lines you care about.
Ask your commissioner to raise a specific change before the rate cap vote.

milestones.influenceWhy: The draft now exists, so specific asks are possible, and the rate cap has not been voted yet.

milestones.name: Early budget workshops
milestones.output: Direction to staff before the rate cap is set

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually June or July. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend and speak if the workshop takes comment.
Email the commission before the workshop with a specific line item.

milestones.influenceWhy: Officials are still shaping the plan and can be moved before the July rate vote.

milestones.name: Commission sets the proposed (maximum) tax rate and first hearing date
milestones.output: Proposed millage, rolled-back rate and first hearing date sent to the Property Appraiser (DR-420)

timing.rule: Within 35 days of certification (day 35 is about August 4). A body that misses it cannot levy above the rolled-back rate.

residentCan.how: Speak at the July meeting where the proposed rate is voted.
Write to each commissioner before the vote asking for a specific rate, such as the rolled-back rate.
Call your district office the week of the vote.

milestones.influenceWhy: This rate goes on every TRIM notice and in practice caps the September rate; raising it later needs a new mailed notice to every taxpayer.

milestones.name: Budget workshops and town halls
milestones.output: Changes the commission asks for before the hearings

timing.rule: Set by each body, usually August. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend the town hall or workshop and ask about a specific line.
Email questions in advance so staff answer them in the room.

milestones.influenceWhy: Spending lines can still move, but the rate cap is already set.

milestones.name: TRIM notices mailed to property owners
inputs: Proposed rates and hearing dates from every taxing authority
milestones.output: Notice of Proposed Property Taxes (TRIM notice) to every owner

timing.rule: By the later of 55 days after certification (about August 24) or 10 days after the roll is approved.

residentCan.how: Check your notice: it lists each body's proposed rate and hearing date. To appeal your assessed value, petition the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the mailing (s. 194.011(3)(d), F.S.).
Use the hearing date on the notice to plan to speak.

milestones.influenceWhy: Turns the July rate into a dollar figure owners can see; strong turnout at the first hearing starts here.

milestones.name: Tentative budget posted online
milestones.output: Tentative budget on the official website

timing.rule: At least 5 days before the first budget hearing, and kept online at least 45 days.

residentCan.how: Download the tentative budget and compare it with the proposed one.

milestones.influenceWhy: Last look at the numbers before the hearing that fixes the ceiling.

milestones.name: First public budget hearing (tentative rate and budget)
milestones.output: Tentative millage and tentative budget adopted

timing.rule: Between day 65 and day 80 after certification (about September 3 to 18), after 5 p.m. on a weekday. The first item is the percent increase over the rolled-back rate. The county may not use a School Board hearing date; cities may not use county or School Board dates.

residentCan.how: Speak at the hearing: the public must be heard before any vote.
Send written comments before the hearing so they are in the record.

milestones.influenceWhy: The tentative rate set here is the most the final rate can be; the final hearing can only hold or lower it.

milestones.name: Final hearing advertised
milestones.output: Newspaper notice of the final hearing with a budget summary (Notice of Proposed Tax Increase if above rolled-back rate)

timing.rule: Within 15 days after the first hearing.

residentCan.how: Read the notice and send comments before the final hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: A notice, not a decision.

milestones.name: Final public budget hearing (final rate and budget)
milestones.output: Final millage and budget adopted, rate first, by separate votes

timing.rule: Not less than 2 nor more than 5 days after the ad first runs. The final rate may not exceed the tentative rate.

residentCan.how: Speak at the final hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The rate can still go down here, but not up, and most lines were settled at the first hearing.

milestones.name: Mayor may veto budget items
milestones.output: Veto message, or the budget stands

timing.rule: Within 10 days of final adoption. The Commission may override by two thirds of members present at its next regular meeting.

residentCan.how: Ask the Mayor's office to veto or keep a specific item within the 10 days.

milestones.influenceWhy: Rarely used and limited: vetoing revenue requires vetoing equal spending.

milestones.name: Adopted rate sent to Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
milestones.output: Rate on file for the November tax bills

timing.rule: Within 3 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the adopted millage resolution or ordinance.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork after the decision.

milestones.name: Fiscal year begins
milestones.output: Budget in effect October 1 to September 30

timing.rule: October 1.

residentCan.how: Watch for budget amendments during the year; they are adopted the same way as the budget.

milestones.influenceWhy: The budget is set; changes come only by amendment.

milestones.name: Certification of TRIM compliance to the state
milestones.output: Form DR-487 filed with the Florida Department of Revenue

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-487 package to check the ads and votes followed the law.

milestones.influenceWhy: A compliance filing; problems found here go to the Department of Revenue.

milestones.name: Final budget posted online
milestones.output: Adopted budget on the official website for at least 5 years

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Download the adopted budget to track spending during the year.

milestones.influenceWhy: Publication of a decision already made.

annual-budget-and-millage-school-distric.name: Yearly school budget and property tax rate (school district)
annual-budget-and-millage-school-distric.summary: School districts run on a faster TRIM clock: the tentative budget hearing is in late July, before TRIM notices go out. Most of the school tax rate is the required local effort set by the state; the board sets the discretionary rates.
annual-budget-and-millage-school-distric.dayCounting: Same day counting as the regular TRIM template: the later of July 1 or certification is day 1 (s. 200.065(12), F.S.).

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for school districts, Florida DOR

milestones.name: Board budget workshops
milestones.output: Direction for the tentative budget

timing.rule: Set by the board, usually May and June. Not set by state law.

residentCan.how: Attend the workshop; ask the board to raise a specific priority.
Send written comments through the Citizen Information Center before the workshop.

milestones.influenceWhy: The last open stage before the tentative budget is drafted; the July ad and hearing then come within days.

milestones.name: Property Appraiser certifies school taxable value
milestones.output: Certification of School Taxable Value (Form DR-420S)

timing.rule: July 1 or the certification date, whichever is later, is day 1.

residentCan.how: Read the DR-420S to see the rolled-back rate.

milestones.influenceWhy: A valuation, not a board choice.

milestones.name: School fiscal year begins
milestones.output: District spends on ordinary expenses until the tentative budget becomes official

timing.rule: July 1. State law lets boards pay ordinary expenses from July 1 until the budget is official.

residentCan.how: Ask what the district is spending under the interim authority.

milestones.influenceWhy: Automatic.

milestones.name: State sets required local effort tax rate
inputs: Department of Revenue estimate of school taxable value
milestones.output: Required local effort millage certified to the board

timing.rule: Not later than July 19.

residentCan.how: This rate is set in Tallahassee; contact your state legislators about it, not the School Board.

milestones.influenceWhy: Set by the state; the board must levy it.

milestones.name: Superintendent submits the tentative budget
milestones.output: Tentative budget and proposed millage to the board

timing.rule: No later than 24 days after certification (about July 24).

residentCan.how: Read the tentative budget when it is posted with the July agenda.

milestones.influenceWhy: The draft exists; specific asks to board members can still change it before the hearing.

milestones.name: Tentative budget and tax rate advertised
milestones.output: Notice of the tentative budget hearing with a budget summary (Notice of Proposed Tax Increase if above rolled-back rate)

timing.rule: Within 29 days after certification (about July 29).

residentCan.how: Speak at the July regular meeting where the board authorizes the ad.

milestones.influenceWhy: The proposed rate becomes public here; the hearing follows within days.

milestones.name: Tentative budget posted online
milestones.output: Tentative budget on the district website

timing.rule: At least 2 days before the tentative budget hearing.

residentCan.how: Download it and bring specific questions to the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Last look before the hearing that sets the ceiling.

milestones.name: Tentative budget hearing
milestones.output: Tentative millage and budget adopted

timing.rule: Not less than 2 nor more than 5 days after the ad runs.

residentCan.how: Register to speak by the deadline for special meetings and speak at the hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Sets the tentative rate that goes on TRIM notices and caps the September rate.

milestones.name: Proposed rate sent to Property Appraiser
milestones.output: Proposed rate, rolled-back rate and final hearing date for the TRIM notice

timing.rule: Within 35 days of certification (about August 4).

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-420S as filed.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork carrying the July decision.

milestones.name: TRIM notices mailed
inputs: Proposed rates from every taxing authority
milestones.output: Notice of Proposed Property Taxes to every owner

timing.rule: By about 55 days after certification.

residentCan.how: Check the school line on your notice. Appeal your assessed value to the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of mailing (s. 194.011(3)(d), F.S.).

milestones.influenceWhy: Shows owners the school tax in dollars before the final hearing.

milestones.name: Final budget hearing
milestones.output: Final millage and budget adopted

timing.rule: Between day 65 and day 80 after certification (about September 3 to 18). No newspaper ad is required before it.

residentCan.how: Speak at the final hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The rate can be held or lowered here, not raised above the tentative rate.

milestones.name: Adopted rate sent to Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
milestones.output: Rate on file for tax bills

timing.rule: Within 3 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask for the adopted millage resolution.

milestones.influenceWhy: Paperwork.

milestones.name: Certification of TRIM compliance to the state
milestones.output: Form DR-487 filed with the Department of Revenue

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

legalBasis.cite: TRIM timetable for school districts, Florida DOR (DR-487)

residentCan.how: Ask for the DR-487 package.

milestones.influenceWhy: Compliance filing.

milestones.name: Final budget posted online
milestones.output: Adopted budget on the district website

timing.rule: Within 30 days after adoption.

residentCan.how: Download the adopted budget.

milestones.influenceWhy: Publication of a decision already made.

election-to-office-county-and-school.name: County Commission and School Board elections
election-to-office-county-and-school.summary: Nonpartisan seats elected by district in the August primary of even years; if no one wins a majority, the top two meet in a runoff on the November general election ballot. New terms start the second Tuesday after the general election.
election-to-office-county-and-school.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor; "29 days before" is offset -29.

milestones.name: Candidate qualifying
milestones.actor: Candidates, filing with the Supervisor of Elections
milestones.output: Who is on the ballot

timing.rule: Noon of the 71st day to noon of the 67th day before the primary.

residentCan.how: Run: file papers and the fee, or petition signatures by the earlier petition deadline.

milestones.influenceWhy: Decides who you can choose from.

milestones.name: Campaign finance reports
milestones.output: Public reports: every other Friday from the 60th day before the primary to the 4th day before the general, plus reports on the 25th and 11th days before each election

timing.rule: Quarterly, then on the pre-election schedule; the filing officer publishes exact dates.

residentCan.how: Read who is funding each candidate on the Supervisor of Elections site.

milestones.influenceWhy: Lets voters weigh who funds a candidate before voting.

milestones.name: Primary election
milestones.output: Winner with a majority, or top two to the runoff

timing.rule: The Tuesday 11 weeks before the general election.

residentCan.how: Vote; nonpartisan races are open to all registered voters.

milestones.influenceWhy: Many seats are decided outright here.

milestones.name: Voter registration closes
milestones.output: Voter roll for the election

timing.rule: 29 days before the election.

residentCan.how: Register or update your address by this date.

milestones.influenceWhy: Miss it and you cannot vote in this election.

milestones.name: Last day to request a mail ballot
milestones.output: Mail ballot sent

timing.rule: 5 p.m. on the 12th day before the election.

residentCan.how: Request a mail ballot by this deadline; it must be received by 7 p.m. on election day (s. 101.67(2), F.S.).

milestones.influenceWhy: Keeps the mail option open.

milestones.name: Early voting
milestones.output: Votes cast in person before election day

timing.rule: Required from the 10th to the 3rd day before the election; the Supervisor may add any of the 15th to 11th days and the 2nd day, so the outer limit is the 15th to the 2nd day.

residentCan.how: Vote early at any early voting site in the county.

milestones.influenceWhy: Your vote is the decision.

milestones.name: General election (runoff)
milestones.output: Winner

timing.rule: The first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even years.

residentCan.how: Vote at your precinct, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

milestones.influenceWhy: Your vote is the decision.

milestones.name: Unofficial results due
milestones.output: First unofficial returns

timing.rule: Noon on the 4th day after a general election.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public.

milestones.influenceWhy: A count, not a choice.

milestones.name: Recount if the margin is close
milestones.output: Machine recount at 0.5% or less; manual recount of over and under votes at 0.25% or less

timing.rule: After unofficial results; the trailing candidate may waive.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public; you may observe.

milestones.influenceWhy: A count, not a choice.

milestones.name: Official results certified
milestones.output: Certified winners

timing.rule: Noon on the 13th day after a general election.

residentCan.how: Read the certified precinct results.

milestones.influenceWhy: A count, not a choice.

milestones.name: Election contest window
milestones.output: Contest filed in circuit court, or results stand

timing.rule: Within 10 days after certification.

residentCan.how: A qualified voter may file a contest in circuit court within 10 days of certification.

milestones.influenceWhy: Rare and costly.

milestones.name: New terms begin
milestones.output: Members take office

timing.rule: The second Tuesday after the general election.

residentCan.how: Introduce yourself to the new member's office and name your top issue.

milestones.influenceWhy: New members set staff and priorities in their first weeks.

milestones.name: Campaign accounts closed and final report
milestones.output: Disposition of surplus funds reported

timing.rule: Within 90 days after the candidate is elected, eliminated or unopposed.

residentCan.how: Read the final report to see where leftover money went.

milestones.influenceWhy: After the fact, but it shows who funded the winner.

election-to-office-municipal.name: City elections
election-to-office-municipal.summary: City charters set qualifying, election and runoff dates and when terms begin. State law still sets registration, mail ballot, campaign finance, recount and contest rules.
election-to-office-municipal.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor; "29 days before" is offset -29.

milestones.name: Candidate qualifying
milestones.actor: Candidates, filing with the City Clerk
milestones.output: Who is on the ballot

timing.rule: Set by the city charter or code; the city may change it by ordinance.

residentCan.how: Run: file with the City Clerk during the window.

milestones.influenceWhy: Decides who you can choose from.

milestones.name: Campaign finance reports
milestones.output: Public reports filed with the City Clerk on the state schedule

timing.rule: The City Clerk gives each candidate the schedule; cities may not adopt a different one.

residentCan.how: Read the reports on the clerk's site or ask the clerk.

milestones.influenceWhy: Lets voters weigh who funds a candidate before voting.

milestones.name: Voter registration closes
milestones.output: Voter roll for the election

timing.rule: 29 days before the election.

residentCan.how: Register or update your address by this date.

milestones.influenceWhy: Miss it and you cannot vote in this election.

milestones.name: Last day to request a mail ballot
milestones.output: Mail ballot sent

timing.rule: 5 p.m. on the 12th day before the election.

residentCan.how: Request a mail ballot by this deadline; it must be received by 7 p.m. on election day (s. 101.67(2), F.S.).

milestones.influenceWhy: Keeps the mail option open.

milestones.name: Early voting
milestones.actor: Supervisor of Elections or the city
milestones.output: Votes cast before election day

timing.rule: When held with a state election: required from the 10th to the 3rd day before, and the Supervisor may add the 15th to 11th and the 2nd day. A city election held alone may offer early voting at its own sites.

residentCan.how: Vote early at any county early voting site when the city election is on a county ballot.

milestones.influenceWhy: Your vote is the decision.

milestones.name: City election
milestones.output: Winner, or a runoff where the charter requires a majority

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Vote, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

milestones.influenceWhy: Your vote is the decision.

milestones.name: Recount if the margin is close
milestones.output: Machine recount at 0.5% or less; manual recount of over and under votes at 0.25% or less

timing.rule: After unofficial results; the trailing candidate may waive.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public; you may observe.

milestones.influenceWhy: A count, not a choice.

milestones.name: Official results certified
milestones.output: Certified winners

timing.rule: Set by the city charter or code and the canvassing board.

residentCan.how: Read the certified results.

milestones.influenceWhy: A count, not a choice.

milestones.name: Election contest window
milestones.output: Contest filed in circuit court, or results stand

timing.rule: Within 10 days after certification.

residentCan.how: A qualified voter may file a contest in circuit court within 10 days of certification.

milestones.influenceWhy: Rare and costly.

milestones.name: Runoff election (if needed)
milestones.output: Winner

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Vote in the runoff; registration closes 29 days before it.

milestones.influenceWhy: Runoffs often have low turnout, so each vote weighs more.

milestones.name: New terms begin
milestones.output: Members take office

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Introduce yourself to the new member and name your top issue.

milestones.influenceWhy: New members set priorities in their first weeks.

milestones.name: Campaign accounts closed and final report
milestones.output: Disposition of surplus funds reported

timing.rule: Within 90 days after the candidate is elected, eliminated or unopposed.

residentCan.how: Read the final report to see where leftover money went.

milestones.influenceWhy: After the fact, but it shows who funded the winner.

ordinance-adoption-municipal.name: City ordinance adoption
ordinance-adoption-municipal.summary: How a city passes a local law: two readings on separate days, a published notice at least 10 days before adoption, and a business impact estimate for most ordinances. Rezonings and use-list changes add mailed notice or two advertised hearings.
ordinance-adoption-municipal.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor.

milestones.name: Ordinance drafted and placed on an agenda
milestones.actor: Commission member, City Manager or City Attorney
inputs: Request from a member, staff or applicant
milestones.output: Written ordinance with one subject stated in its title

timing.rule: Any time; set by the body's agenda deadlines.

residentCan.how: Ask the sponsor or the City Attorney for the draft and suggest changes before it is public.
Request drafts and related emails.

milestones.influenceWhy: Wording is easiest to change before the text is on an agenda.

milestones.name: Local Planning Agency review
milestones.output: Recommendation on consistency with the comprehensive plan

timing.rule: Before the commission acts on a land development regulation; set by the city code.

residentCan.how: Speak at the planning board hearing.
Send comments to the planning department for the staff report.

milestones.influenceWhy: Board recommendations shape the commission vote and the record for any later appeal.

milestones.name: First reading
milestones.output: Ordinance passed on first reading (or changed, deferred or killed)

timing.rule: A regular or special meeting. The ordinance must be read on at least 2 separate days.

residentCan.how: Speak on the item at the meeting.
Write to the commission before the meeting.

milestones.influenceWhy: Amendments are most common between first and second reading.

milestones.name: Business impact estimate posted
milestones.output: Estimate of direct costs to for-profit businesses and number affected, on the city website

timing.rule: No later than the day the notice of adoption is published. Not required for budgets, procurement, emergency, contract or grant, debt, state-required, and certain development ordinances.

residentCan.how: Read the estimate on the city website; ask for the backup if it looks thin.
Point out costs the estimate missed before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Puts the business cost on the record before the vote.

milestones.name: Notice of proposed enactment published
milestones.output: Newspaper or website notice with date, time, place and where to read the ordinance

timing.rule: At least 10 days before adoption.

residentCan.how: Inspect the ordinance where the notice says.

milestones.influenceWhy: A notice, but it starts the clock to prepare comments.

milestones.name: Mailed notice to owners (small city-initiated rezoning)
inputs: Owner list from the tax roll
milestones.output: Letter to each affected owner

timing.rule: At least 30 days before the hearing.

residentCan.how: If you get a letter, plan to speak at the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Gives owners a month to organize.

milestones.name: First advertised hearing (use-list change or 10 or more acres)
inputs: Display ad, not in the legal notices section
milestones.output: First of two hearings

timing.rule: At least 7 days after the first ad. At least one of the two hearings is after 5 p.m. on a weekday unless a majority plus one votes otherwise.

residentCan.how: Speak at the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Changes to what can be built are made between the two hearings.

milestones.name: Second reading and public hearing (adoption)
milestones.output: Ordinance adopted by majority of members present, each vote recorded

timing.rule: A separate day from first reading. For a use-list change or 10 or more acres, at least 10 days after the first hearing.

residentCan.how: Speak at the public hearing.
Send written comments before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The last public chance, but positions are often settled by now.

milestones.name: Ordinance takes effect
milestones.output: Local law in force

timing.rule: 10 days after passage unless the ordinance says otherwise.

residentCan.how: Where the charter allows, a referendum petition can ask voters to repeal it.
Check the city charter for the signature threshold and deadline.

milestones.influenceWhy: Only a referendum petition or a new ordinance changes it now.

ordinance-adoption-county.name: County ordinance adoption
ordinance-adoption-county.summary: How the County Commission passes an ordinance: first reading by title, committee review, a published notice, a public hearing at second reading, then a 10-day Mayor veto window.
ordinance-adoption-county.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor.

milestones.name: Ordinance drafted and sponsored
milestones.actor: Commissioner or Mayor, with the County Attorney
inputs: Request from a commissioner, the Mayor or staff
milestones.output: Written ordinance with a title and enacting clause

timing.rule: Any time; set by agenda printing deadlines.

residentCan.how: Ask the sponsoring commissioner's office for the draft and suggest changes.
Request drafts and backup from the Clerk of the Board.

milestones.influenceWhy: Wording is easiest to change before first reading.

milestones.name: First reading (title only)
milestones.output: Ordinance set for committee and public hearing

timing.rule: A regular meeting. Read by title only; no debate except under the general comment rule.

residentCan.how: Use the general comment period (Rule 6.06) at the start of the meeting.

milestones.influenceWhy: Mostly procedural, but it starts the public clock.

milestones.name: Committee review and hearing
inputs: Fiscal impact and social equity statements
milestones.output: Recommendation: favorable, with amendments, no recommendation, or report only

timing.rule: After first reading, at the committee the Chair assigns. Deferral is limited to two meetings in a row.

residentCan.how: Speak at the committee meeting if the committee takes testimony.
Reach committee members before the meeting.

milestones.influenceWhy: Most amendments happen in committee, before the full board.

milestones.name: Business impact estimate posted
milestones.output: Estimate of direct costs to for-profit businesses, on the county website

timing.rule: No later than the day the notice is published. Exemptions include budgets, procurement, emergency, contract or grant, debt, state-required and certain development ordinances.

residentCan.how: Point out costs the estimate missed before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: Puts the business cost on the record before the vote.

milestones.name: Notice of intent published
milestones.output: Published notice with date, time, place and where to read the text

timing.rule: At least 10 days before the hearing (state law); the charter also requires a summary at least one week before. Ordinances that directly affect cities wait at least six weeks after first reading.

residentCan.how: Read the ordinance where the notice says.

milestones.influenceWhy: A notice, but it starts the clock to prepare comments.

milestones.name: Public hearing and second reading (adoption)
milestones.output: Ordinance adopted, amended or rejected by individual vote

timing.rule: At a noticed regular meeting; public hearings are set for 9:30 a.m.

residentCan.how: Register at least 15 minutes before the item; up to 5 minutes to speak.
Write to your district commissioner before the hearing.

milestones.influenceWhy: The last public chance; votes are often settled after committee.

milestones.name: Mayor may veto
milestones.output: Veto, or the ordinance stands; override needs two thirds of members present at the next regular meeting

timing.rule: Within 10 days of adoption.

residentCan.how: Ask the Mayor's office to veto or sign within the 10 days.

rule-adoption-school-district.name: School Board policy adoption
rule-adoption-school-district.summary: School boards do not pass ordinances; they adopt policies (rules) under ch. 120, F.S.: first reading, a published notice, a written comment period, then final action.
rule-adoption-school-district.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor.

milestones.name: Policy change drafted
inputs: Board request, new state law or staff proposal
milestones.output: Draft policy for first reading

timing.rule: Any time.

residentCan.how: Ask your Board member to sponsor or change a policy before it is drafted.

milestones.influenceWhy: Wording is easiest to change before first reading.

milestones.name: First reading and authority to give notice
milestones.output: Board authorizes notice of the proposed rule

timing.rule: A regular meeting.

residentCan.how: Register to speak on the item.

milestones.influenceWhy: The text is public and the comment period is about to open.

milestones.name: Notice of proposed rule published
milestones.output: Notice in a local newspaper or on a public website, mailed to people who asked

timing.rule: At least 28 days before final action.

residentCan.how: Ask to be on the mailing list for rule notices.

milestones.influenceWhy: Opens the formal comment and hearing-request window.

milestones.name: Deadline to request a public hearing
milestones.output: Board must schedule a hearing if one is requested

timing.rule: Within 21 days after the notice.

residentCan.how: Send written comments during the period.
Request a public hearing in writing within 21 days of the notice.

milestones.influenceWhy: A written request forces a hearing on the rule.

milestones.name: Final action
milestones.output: Policy adopted, changed or withdrawn

timing.rule: A regular meeting at least 28 days after the notice.

residentCan.how: Speak on the item at the meeting.

milestones.influenceWhy: Last chance; changes after notice can require a new notice.

procurement-award.name: Contract award (procurement)
procurement-award.summary: How a public contract is bought: a solicitation, sealed responses, an evaluation, a written recommendation, a protest window, and the award vote. In Miami-Dade a Cone of Silence limits oral contact with officials while the solicitation is open.
procurement-award.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days unless offsetUnit says business days.

legalBasis.cite: Miami-Dade County Code Sec. 2-11.1(t) (Cone of Silence)

milestones.name: Need identified and funded
milestones.output: Funded project or service ready to buy

timing.rule: Usually through the yearly budget.

residentCan.how: Speak at budget hearings about the project.
Ask your commissioner whether the project is in the capital plan.

milestones.influenceWhy: Whether to buy at all is decided in the budget.

milestones.name: Scope and evaluation criteria written
milestones.output: Draft ITB, RFP or RFQ with scope and scoring criteria

timing.rule: Before advertisement; set by the body's procurement code.

residentCan.how: Ask the department or your commissioner about scope (for example local hiring or service levels) before the solicitation is advertised.
Request the draft scope.

milestones.influenceWhy: Scope and scoring decide the outcome, and they are fixed once advertised.

milestones.name: Solicitation advertised; Cone of Silence begins
milestones.output: Public ITB, RFP or RFQ; oral contact about it with officials is restricted

timing.rule: Set by the body's code. For architecture and engineering services, public notice of the need is required.

residentCan.how: Write to officials: in the county, written messages copied to the Clerk of the Board are allowed at all times.

milestones.influenceWhy: Terms are public but fixed; addenda can still change them.

milestones.name: Bids or proposals opened
milestones.output: List of bidders; contents stay confidential for a time

timing.rule: The due date in the solicitation.

residentCan.how: Ask for the bidder list now and the full responses once they become public.

milestones.influenceWhy: A fact-finding step.

milestones.name: Evaluation or selection committee scores responses
milestones.output: Ranking

timing.rule: After opening. Vendor presentations and negotiations are closed but must be recorded.

residentCan.how: Ask for score sheets and the recordings once the exemption ends (notice of intended decision or 30 days after opening).

milestones.influenceWhy: Residents cannot take part, but the record becomes public.

milestones.name: Written award recommendation; Cone of Silence ends
milestones.output: Recommendation on the commission agenda

timing.rule: When the recommendation is issued. Sealed responses must become public by now or 30 days after opening, whichever is earlier.

residentCan.how: Now officials may discuss it openly: call or write before the vote.
Get the full responses and scoring.
Send written comments for the agenda item.

milestones.influenceWhy: The choice is public and not yet voted; this is the window to question it.

milestones.name: Bid protest window
milestones.setBy: The body's procurement code; school districts follow s. 120.57(3), F.S.
inputs: Recommendation or notice of intended decision
milestones.output: Protest filed (award paused) or window closes

timing.rule: Short, and set by the body's procurement code or implementing order.

residentCan.how: Ask the clerk whether a protest was filed; protests are public records.

milestones.influenceWhy: Only bidders can protest.

milestones.name: Award vote
milestones.output: Contract awarded, rejected or sent back

timing.rule: A regular meeting after the protest window. Awards under the delegated limit are made by the Mayor or Manager without a vote.

residentCan.how: Speak on the award item.
Send written comments before the meeting.

milestones.influenceWhy: Officials can still reject or send it back, but rarely do.

milestones.name: Contract signed
milestones.output: Signed contract

timing.rule: After award.

residentCan.how: Ask for the signed contract and later amendments and change orders.

milestones.influenceWhy: Decided; watch for change orders.

meetingPattern.text: Regular meetings about once a month, usually a Wednesday at 11:00 a.m., in the School Board Administration Building Auditorium, 1450 NE 2nd Avenue, Miami 33132. The public hearing for non-agenda topics follows the regular agenda and begins no later than about 6:30 p.m. Budget hearings are evening special meetings at 6:00 p.m. Workshops (budget, safety) are usually 10:00 a.m. The Board sets each year's schedule at its November Organization Meeting.
